newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt orders PTT to study LPG oversupply.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt orders PTT to study LPG oversupply.

text.p: The Thai government asked state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand to urgently map out measures to deal with an oversupply of liquefied petroleum gas, a government official said on Monday.
The move was recommended by the government think-tank--the National Economic and Social Development Board.
"The government is concerned after the official estimates suggested the output will rise 56 percent over last year," the official said.

The industry forecast that LPG output would rise sharply this year due to additional output from PTT's third natural gas separation plant and from the country's two new oil refineries which came onstream last year.
The commerce ministry projected that local LPG production this year would rise 56 percent over last year to an average of 8,029 tonnes a day.

Domestic demand, on the other hand, was expected to grow by only 18 percent to an average of 5,488 tonnes a day. Of this, 5,128 tonnes will be used as fuel and the rest as feedstock for local petrochemical industries.
"The government wanted to know what should be done with the excess," she said.

PTT's third gas separation plant, which was built in 1994, reached its full capacity at the end of last month with annual production capacity of 401,400 tonnes of LPG and 117,400 tonnes of methane, according to a PTT official.
Thailand also faced an LPG oversupply last year, but to a much lesser extent, and had to export an average of 538 tonnes per day to Laos, Cambodia and China.
